title: Loans and paying them back
summary: Growth in Supermarket Simulator can be financed rather than saved for: the game has bank credit, a loan status, a payments tab and a bankruptcy path if the money runs out.
body: Credit is its own object in the game, so a loan is a state you carry rather than a one-off menu choice.
The game tracks whether a loan is current, which is why the interface can show a status for it and give repayments their own tab.
There is a bankruptcy path as well: the game defines bankruptcy handling and a screen for it, so failing to pay is a situation the game anticipates.
What this entry does not tell you: interest rates, repayment schedules, borrowing limits or what exactly triggers bankruptcy. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Borrowing is a defined object in the game.
A loan carries a status the game tracks.
Repayments have their own interface tab.
The game has a bankruptcy path and its own screen for it.
The loan screen names a daily payment object of its own, with a label beside it.
facts.evidence: asset names: Daily Payment, Daily Payment Text

facts.claim: The loan screen ships its own amount and daily-interest labels along with a repayment item.
facts.evidence: asset names: Loan Amount Text, Daily Interest, Loan Repayment Item

facts.claim: Borrowing has a term length of its own, with a slider and a text field for it, and the screen names a loan button.
facts.evidence: asset names: Loan Term Length Slider, Loan Term Length Text, Loan Button
